  3102                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  3103                                  
  3104                                  ;============================================================================
  3105                                  ; MSHEAD.ASM (MSDOS 6.0, 1991)
  3106                                  ;============================================================================
  3107                                  ; 16/07/2018 - Retro DOS 3.0
  3108                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3109                                  ; 24/04/2019 - Retro DOS 4.0
  3110                                  
  3111                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
  3112                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3113                                  ; FILE : ORIGIN.INC
  3114                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3115                                  ; This is included in origin.asm and mshead.asm. Contains the equate that
  3116                                  ; is used for ORGing the DOS code.
  3117                                  ;
  3118                                  ; Brief Description of the necessacity of this ORG:
  3119                                  ; -------------------------------------------------
  3120                                  ;
  3121                                  ; A special problem exits when running out of the HMA. The HMA starts at 
  3122                                  ; address FFFF:10. There is no place in the HMA with an offset of zero.
  3123                                  ; This means programs running out off the HMA must use non-zero offset base
  3124                                  ; addresses. It also means that if we're running multiple programs from the
  3125                                  ; HMA, the base offset of each segment must atleast be as big as all of the
  3126                                  ; HMA segments that precede it.
  3127                                  ; 
  3128                                  ; One solution to this problem to ORG each module at 64K minus its size.
  3129                                  ; For instance a code segment 1234h bytes in length would org'd at edcbh.
  3130                                  ; This gives max. flexibility regarding it's location in the HMA. By 
  3131                                  ; selecting segment values between f124h and ffffh it could be located 
  3132                                  ; anywhere in the HMA. The problem with this is that programs with such 
  3133                                  ; high ORGs would not be able to run in low RAM.
  3134                                  ;
  3135                                  ; A compromise solution is to set the ORG address somewhere between 0010h
  3136                                  ; and ffffh - their size. In the particular case of the BIOS and the DOS 
  3137                                  ; the following solution has been implemented:
  3138                                  ;
  3139                                  ; The Bios Code segment will have a very small offset and run at the very
  3140                                  ; front of the HMA, after the VDISK header. THE Dos Code segment will have 
  3141                                  ; a base offset of (700+<min. size off RAM based BIOS>+<min. size of the DOS
  3142                                  ; DATA segment when DOS is running low>). This will reflect the lowest 
  3143                                  ; possible physical address at which DOS code will run, while still providing
  3144                                  ; max. possible flexibility in HMA positioning. This offset MUST NOT be 
  3145                                  ; smaller then that 20+size of Bios Code segment when running high. This is 
  3146                                  ; mostly true.
  3147                                  ;
  3148                                  ; Also this ORG'd value must be communicated to the BIOS. This is done by
  3149                                  ; putting this value after the first jmp instruction in the DOS code in
  3150                                  ; mshead.asm. 
  3151                                  ;
  3152                                  ; In order for the stripz utility to know how many zeroes to be stripped 
  3153                                  ; out, this value is placed at the beginning of the binary in origin.asm.
  3154                                  ;
  3155                                  ; Revision History:
  3156                                  ;
  3157                                  ; Currently this is being done manually. Therefore any change in the DOS DATA
  3158                                  ; Size or the BIOS size should be reflected here. --- Feb 90
  3159                                  ;
  3160                                  ; BDSIZE.INC contains the equates for BIODATASIZE, BIOCODESIZ and DOSDATASIZ.
  3161                                  ; A utility called getsize will obtain the corresponding values from msdos
  3162                                  ; and msbio.map and update the values in BDSIZ.INC if they are different. 
  3163                                  ; DOS should now be built using the batch file makedos.bat which invokes this
  3164                                  ; utility. The FORMAT of BDSIZE.INC should not be changed as getsize is 
  3165                                  ; dependant on that.				  --- Apr 3 '90
  3166                                  ;
  3167                                  ; For ROMDOS, however, there is no need to org the doscode to any location
  3168                                  ; other than zero.  Therefore the stripz utility will not need to be used,
  3169                                  ; so the offset will not need to be included at the beginning of the code
  3170                                  ; segment.  Also, the BIOS can just assume that the resident code begins
  3171                                  ; at offset zero within the segment.
  3172                                  ; 
  3173                                  ;
  3174                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3175                                  
  3176                                  BIODATASTART	EQU	00700h
  3177                                  ;include	bdsize.inc	; this sets the values:
  3178                                  				;	BIODATASIZ
  3179                                  				;	BIOCODESIZ
  3180                                  				;	DOSDATASIZ
  3181                                  
  3182                                  ; 05/12/2022
  3183                                  ;BIODATASIZ EQU 00910H	; 0900h for MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS
  3184                                  			; 0900h for MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS
  3185                                  ;BIOCODESIZ EQU 01A70H	; 1A70h for MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS
  3186                                  			; 1A60h for MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS
  3187                                  ;DOSDATASIZ EQU 01370H	; 1370h for MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS
  3188                                  			; 1370h for MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS
  3189                                  ;ifndef ROMDOS
  3190                                  ;
  3191                                  ;BYTSTART	EQU    	BIODATASTART+BIODATASIZ+BIOCODESIZ+DOSDATASIZ
  3192                                  ;PARASTART	EQU	(BYTSTART + 0FH) AND (NOT 0FH)	
  3193                                  ;
  3194                                  ;else
  3195                                  ;
  3196                                  ;BYTSTART	EQU	0
  3197                                  ;PARASTART	EQU	0
  3198                                  ;
  3199                                  ;endif ; ROMDOS

  3304                                  ;;hkn YRTAB & MONTAB moved to DOSDATA in ms_data.asm
  3305                                  ;	I_am	YRTAB,8,<200,166,200,165,200,165,200,165>   ; [SYSTEM]
  3306                                  ;	I_am	MONTAB,12,<31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31> ; [SYSTEM]

  3309                                  ; YRTAB & MONTAB moved from TABLE segment in ms_table.asm
  3310                                  ;
  3311                                  ;	I_am    YRTAB,8,<200,166,200,165,200,165,200,165>   
  3312                                  ;	I_am    MONTAB,12,<31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31> 
  3313                                  
  3314                                  ; This is the error code mapping table for INT 21 errors. This table defines
  3315                                  ; those error codes which are "allowed" for each system call. If the error
  3316                                  ; code ABOUT to be returned is not "allowed" for the call, the correct action
  3317                                  ; is to return the "real" error via Extended error, and one of the allowed
  3318                                  ; errors on the actual call.
  3319                                  ;
  3320                                  ; The table is organized as follows:
  3321                                  ;
  3322                                  ;    Each entry in the table is of variable size, but the first
  3323                                  ;       two bytes are always:
  3324                                  ;
  3325                                  ;       Call#,Cnt of bytes following this byte
  3326                                  ;
  3327                                  ; EXAMPLE:
  3328                                  ;       Call 61 (OPEN)
  3329                                  ;
  3330                                  ;       DB      61,5,12,3,2,4,5
  3331                                  ;
  3332                                  ;       61 is the AH INT 21 call value for OPEN.
  3333                                  ;        5 indicates that there are 5 bytes after this byte (12,3,2,4,5).
  3334                                  ;       Next five bytes are those error codes which are "allowed" on OPEN.
  3335                                  ;       The order of these values is not important EXCEPT FOR THE LAST ONE (in
  3336                                  ;       this case 5).  The last value will be the one returned on the call if
  3337                                  ;       the "real" error is not one of the allowed ones.
  3338                                  ;
  3339                                  ; There are a number of calls (for instance all of the FCB calls) for which
  3340                                  ;   there is NO entry.  This means that NO error codes are returned on this
  3341                                  ;   call, so set up an Extended error and leave the current error code alone.
  3342                                  ;
  3343                                  ; The table is terminated by a call value of 0FFh
  3344                                  
  3345                                  ;PUBLIC I21_MAP_E_TAB
  3346                                  	; 10/08/2018
  3347                                  
  3348                                  ; 29/04/2019
  3349                                  ; DOSCODE:3DE9h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  3350                                  ; 04/11/2022
  3351                                  ; DOSCODE:3DDBh	(MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  3352                                  ; 01/01/2024
  3353                                  ; DOSCODE:3F1Bh	(PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)

  4129                                  ; DOSCODE:40CCh (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  4130                                  
  4131                                  ; ==========================================================================
  4132                                  ;
  4133                                  ; The Quit entry point is where all INT 20h's come from. These are old- style
  4134                                  ; exit system calls. The CS of the caller indicates which Process is dying.
  4135                                  ; The error code is presumed to be 0. We simulate an ABORT system call.
  4136                                  ;
  4137                                  ; ==========================================================================
  4138                                  
  4139                                  SYSTEM_CALL:    ; PROC NEAR
  4140                                  
  4141                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4142                                  ; DOSCODE:40BFh (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
  4143                                  
  4144                                  ;entry	QUIT				
  4145                                  QUIT:				; INT 20H entry point
  4146                                  	;MOV	AH,0
  4147 000002D9 30E4                    	xor	ah,ah ; 08/07/2018
  4148 000002DB EB36                    	JMP     SHORT SAVREGS
  4149                                  
  4150                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4151                                  
  4152                                  	; The system call in AH is out of the range that we know how
  4153                                  	; to handle. We arbitrarily set the contents of AL to 0 and
  4154                                  	; IRET. Note that we CANNOT set the carry flag to indicate an
  4155                                  	; error as this may break some programs compatability.
  4156                                  
  4157                                  BADCALL:
  4158                                          ;MOV	AL,0
  4159 000002DD 30C0                    	xor	al,al ; 08/07/2018
  4160                                  IRETT:	; 06/05/2019
  4161                                  _IRET:
  4162 000002DF CF                              IRET
  4163                                  
  4164                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4165                                  
  4166                                  ; 01/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  4167                                  ; DOSCODE:40D3h (MSDOS 6.21 MSDOS.SYS)
  4168                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4169                                  ; DOSCODE:40C6h (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4170                                  
  4171                                  	; An alternative method of entering the system is to perform a
  4172                                  	; CALL 5 in the program segment prefix with the contents of CL
  4173                                  	; indicating what system call the user would like. A subset of
  4174                                  	; the possible system calls is allowed here only the
  4175                                  	; CPM-compatible calls may get dispatched.
  4176                                  
  4177                                  		; System call entry point and dispatcher
  4178                                  CALL_ENTRY:
  4179 000002E0 1E                      	push	DS
  4180                                  	;getdseg <DS>			; DS -> DosData, ASSUME DS:DosSeg
  4181 000002E1 2E8E1E[0700]            	mov	ds,[cs:DosDSeg]
  4182 000002E6 8F06[EC05]              	pop	word [SAVEDS]		; Save original DS
  4183                                  
  4184 000002EA 58                              POP     AX                      ; IP from the long call at 5
  4185 000002EB 58                              POP     AX                      ; Segment from the long call at 5
  4186 000002EC 8F06[8405]              	POP	WORD [USER_SP]		; IP from the CALL 5
  4187                                  
  4188                                  		; Re-order the stack to simulate an interrupt 21.
  4189                                  
  4190 000002F0 9C                      	PUSHF				; Start re-ordering the stack
  4191 000002F1 FA                      	CLI
  4192 000002F2 50                              PUSH    AX                      ; Save segment
  4193 000002F3 FF36[8405]                      PUSH	WORD [USER_SP]		; Stack now ordered as if INT had been used
  4194                                  	; 04/11/2022
  4195                                  	; DOSCODE:40EAh (MSDOS 6.21 MSDOS.SYS)
  4196                                  	; DOSCODE:40DDh (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4197 000002F7 FF36[EC05]              	push	word [SAVEDS]
  4198 000002FB 1F                      	pop	ds
  4199                                  	;
  4200                                  	;cmp	cl,36
  4201 000002FC 80F924                          CMP     CL,MAXCALL              ; This entry point doesn't get as many calls
  4202 000002FF 77DC                            JA      SHORT BADCALL
  4203 00000301 88CC                            MOV     AH,CL
  4204                                  	; 08/07/2018
  4205 00000303 EB0E                    	jmp	short SAVREGS
  4206                                  
  4207                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4208                                  
  4209                                  ; 01/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  4210                                  ; 01/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0

  4975                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4976                                  ;
  4977                                  ; Procedure Name : ABSDRD
  4978                                  ;
  4979                                  ; Interrupt 25 handler. Performs absolute disk read.
  4980                                  ; Inputs:	AL - 0-based drive number
  4981                                  ;		DS:BX point to destination buffer
  4982                                  ;		CX number of logical sectors to read
  4983                                  ;		DX starting logical sector number (0-based)
  4984                                  ; Outputs:	Original flags still on stack
  4985                                  ;		Carry set
  4986                                  ;		    AH error from BIOS
  4987                                  ;		    AL same as low byte of DI from INT 24
  4988                                  ;
  4989                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4990                                          ;procedure   ABSDRD,FAR
  4991                                  ABSDRD:
  4992                                  	; 15/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  4993                                  	; MSDOS 6.21 (DOSCODE:42E5h)
  4994                                  	; 04/11/2022
  4995                                  	; MSDOS 5.0 (DOSCODE:42D8h)
  4996                                  
  4997                                  	; 02/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
  4998                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:43C4h
  4999                                  	
  5000                                  	;;;
  5001 00000541 30E4                    	xor     ah,ah	; ah=0		; Interrupt 25h handler (ah=0)
  5002 00000543 31F6                    	xor     si,si	; si=0		; clear read/write mode flags
  5003                                  					; (used with INT 21h ax=7305h)
  5004                                  FAT32_ABSDRD:	; ah=1 si=0 cf=0 (jump from '_$FAT32EXT')
  5005                                  	; 25/06/2024
  5006                                  	;cli ; *
  5007                                  	;clc ; not necessary
  5008                                  				; INT 21h
  5009                                  				;	AX = 7305h
  5010                                  				; FAT32 - EXTENDED ABSOLUTE DISK READ/WRITE
  5011                                  				;	CX = FFFFh
  5012                                  				;	DL = drive number (01h=A:, etc.)
  5013                                  				;	SI = read/write mode flags
  5014                                  				;	DS:BX -> disk I/O packet
  5015                                  				;
  5016                                  				; Extended Absolute Disk Read/Write mode flags:
  5017                                  				;
  5018                                  				;	Bit(s)  Description
  5019                                  				;	0	direction (0=read, 1=write)
  5020                                  				;	12-1	reserved (0)
  5021                                  				;	14-13	write type (should be 00 on reads).
  5022                                  				;		00 unknown data.
  5023                                  				;		01 FAT data.
  5024                                  				;		10 directory data.
  5025                                  				;		11 file data
  5026                                  				;	15     reserved (0)
  5027                                  				;
  5028                                  				; Format of disk read/write packet:
  5029                                  				;
  5030                                  				;	Offset Size    Description
  5031                                  				;	00h    DWORD   sector number
  5032                                  				;	04h    WORD    number of sectors to r/w
  5033                                  				;	06h    DWORD   transfer address
  5034                                  				;
  5035                                  				; ref: Ralf Brown's Interrupt List
  5036                                  	;;;
  5037                                  absdrd_1:
  5038                                  	; MSDOS 6.0

  5049 00000551 58                      	pop	ax			; restore AX value
  5050

  5052                                  	; We shall save es on the user stack here. We need to use ES in
  5053                                  	; order to access the DOSDATA variables AbsRdWr_SS/SP at exit
  5054                                  	; time in order to restore the user stack.
  5055                                  
  5056 00000552 06                      	push	es  ; ****		; M072
  5057                                  
  5058                                  	; 25/06/2024

  5075

  5077                                  ;

  5079                                  ; version of the getdseg macro with the SS register! An interrupt will
  5080                                  ; sneak through.
  5081

  5086

  5088                                  ;	mov	ds, cs:[BioDataSeg]
  5089                                  ;	assume	ds:bdata
  5090                                  ;
  5091                                  ;	mov	ss, ds:[DosDataSg]
  5092                                  ;	assume	ss:DOSDATA
  5093                                  ;
  5094                                  ;endif ; ROMDOS
  5095                                  					; 02/01/2024
  5096 0000056B BC[2009]                	MOV	SP,DSKSTACK	 	;"@#IBM:12.01.2003.build_1.32#@ IBMDOS.COM(USA)"
  5097                                  					; (PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)

  5115                                  
  5116                                  	; Here is a gross temporary fix to get around a serious design flaw in
  5117                                  	;  the secondary cache. The secondary cache does not check for media
  5118                                  	;  changed (it should). Hence, you can change disks, do an absolute
  5119                                  	;  read, and get data from the previous disk. To get around this,
  5120                                  	;  we just won't use the secondary cache for absolute disk reads.
  5121                                  	;                                                      -mw 8/5/88

  5224                                  ; Procedure Name : ABSDWRT
  5225                                  ;
  5226                                  ; Interrupt 26 handler. Performs absolute disk write.
  5227                                  ; Inputs:	AL - 0-based drive number

  5251                                  FAT32_ABSDWRT:	; ah=1 si=1 cf=0 (jump from '_$FAT32EXT')
  5252                                  
  5253                                  				; INT 21h
  5254                                  				;	AX = 7305h
  5255                                  				; FAT32 - EXTENDED ABSOLUTE DISK READ/WRITE
  5256                                  				;	CX = FFFFh

  5258                                  				;	SI = read/write mode flags
  5259                                  				;	DS:BX -> disk I/O packet
  5260                                  				;
  5261                                  				; Extended Absolute Disk Read/Write mode flags:
  5262                                  				;
  5263                                  				;	Bit(s)  Description
  5264                                  				;	0	direction (0=read, 1=write)
  5265                                  				;	12-1	reserved (0)
  5266                                  				;	14-13	write type (should be 00 on reads).
  5267                                  				;		00 unknown data.
  5268                                  				;		01 FAT data.
  5269                                  				;		10 directory data.
  5270                                  				;		11 file data
  5271                                  				;	15     reserved (0)
  5272                                  				;
  5273                                  				; Format of disk read/write packet:
  5274                                  				;
  5275                                  				;	Offset Size    Description
  5276                                  				;	00h    DWORD   sector number
  5277                                  				;	04h    WORD    number of sectors to r/w
  5278                                  				;	06h    DWORD   transfer address

  6489                                  ;M044; Start of changes
  6490                                  ; Winoldap has a bug in that its calculations for the Windows memory image
  6491                                  ; to save is off by 1 para. This para can happen to be a Windows arena if the
  6492                                  ; DOS top of memory happens to be at an odd boundary (as is the case when
  6493                                  ; UMBs are present). This is because Windows builds its arenas only at even
  6494                                  ; para boundaries. This arena now gets trashed when Windows is swapped back
  6495                                  ; in leading to a crash. Winoldap issues callouts when it swaps Windows out
  6496                                  ; and back in. We sit on these callouts. On the Windows swapout, we save the
  6497                                  ; last para of the Windows memory block and then restore this para on the
  6498                                  ; Windows swapin callout. 
  6499                                  
  6500                                  getwinlast:

  6861                                  ; DOSMES.ASM (MSDOS 2.11, 1983)
  6862                                  
  6863                                  ; OEMFunction key is expected to process a single function
  6864                                  ;   key input from a device and dispatch to the proper
  6865                                  ;   routines leaving all registers UNTOUCHED.
  6866                                  ;
  6867                                  ; Inputs:   CS, SS are DOSGROUP
  6868                                  ; Outputs:  None. This function is expected to JMP to onw of
  6869                                  ;           the following labels:
  6870                                  ;
  6871                                  ;           GetCh       - ignore the sequence
  6872                                  ;           TwoEsc      - insert an ESCChar in the buffer
  6873                                  ;           ExitIns     - toggle insert mode
  6874                                  ;           EnterIns    - toggle insert mode
  6875                                  ;           BackSp      - move backwards one space
  6876                                  ;           ReEdit      - reedit the line with a new template
  6877                                  ;           KilNew      - discard the current line and start from scratch
  6878                                  ;           CopyLin     - copy the rest of the template into the line
  6879                                  ;           SkipStr     - read the next character and skip to it in the template
  6880                                  ;           CopyStr     - read next char and copy from template to line until char
  6881                                  ;           SkipOne     - advance position in template one character
  6882                                  ;           CopyOne     - copy next character in template into line
  6883                                  ;           CtrlZ       - place a ^Z into the template
  6884                                  ; Registers that are allowed to be modified by this function are:
  6885                                  ;           AX, CX, BP
  6886                                  
  6887                                  ; 13/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  6888                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6889                                  ; DOSCODE:4820h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  6890                                  
  6891                                  ; 05/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  6892                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6893                                  ; DOSCODE:4813h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
  6894                                  
  6895                                  ; 06/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
  6896                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6897                                  ; DOSCODE:4967h (PCDOS 7.1, IBMDOS.COM)
  6898                                  
  6899                                  OEMFunctionKey:
  6900 00000AB0 E8450E                  	CALL	_$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO	; Get the second byte of the sequence
  6901 00000AB3 B10E                    	MOV     CL,ESCTABLEN ; 14	; length of table for scan
  6902 00000AB5 57                      	PUSH    DI                      ; save DI (cannot change it!)
  6903 00000AB6 BF[860A]                	MOV     DI,ESCTAB		; offset of second byte table
  6904 00000AB9 06                      	push	es
  6905 00000ABA 0E                      	push	cs
  6906 00000ABB 07                      	pop	es
  6907 00000ABC F2AE                    	REPNE   SCASB                   ; Look it up in the table
  6908 00000ABE 07                      	pop	es
  6909 00000ABF 5F                      	POP     DI                      ; restore DI
  6910 00000AC0 D1E1                    	SHL     CX,1                    ; convert byte offset to word

  6912                                  	;JMP	word [BP+ESCFUNC]	; Go to the right routine

  7405                                  _$GET_VERSION:
  7406                                  
  7407                                  ; Inputs:
  7408                                  ;       None
  7409                                  ; Function:
  7410                                  ;       Return MS-DOS version number
  7411                                  ; Outputs:
  7412                                  ;       OEM number in BH
  7413                                  ;       User number in BL:CX (24 bits)
  7414                                  ;       Version number as AL.AH in binary
  7415                                  ;       NOTE: On pre 1.28 DOSs AL will be zero
  7416                                  
  7417                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
  7418                                  ;
  7419                                  ;	Fake_Count is used to lie about the version numbers to support
  7420                                  ;	old binarys. See ms_table.asm for more info.
  7421                                  ;
  7422                                  ;		if input al = 00
  7423                                  ;		  (bh) = OEM number			
  7424                                  ;		else if input al = 01
  7425                                  ;		  (bh) = version flags
  7426                                  ;		 
  7427                                  ;		       	 bits 0-2 = DOS internal revision
  7428                                  ;		       	 bits 3-7 = DOS type flags
  7429                                  ;		              bit 3    = DOS is in ROM
  7430                                  ;		              bit 4    = DOS in in HMA
  7431                                  ;		              bits 5-7 = reserved
  7432                                  ;               M007 change - only bit 3 is now valid. Other bits
  7433                                  ;               are 0 when AL = 1

  7528                                  ;BREAK <$International - return country-dependent information>
  7529                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  7530                                  ;
  7531                                  ; Procedure Name : $INTERNATIONAL
  7532                                  ;
  7533                                  ; Inputs:
  7534                                  ;	MOV	AH,International
  7535                                  ;	MOV	AL,country	(al = 0 => current country)
  7536                                  ;      [MOV	BX,country]
  7537                                  ;	LDS	DX,block
  7538                                  ;	INT	21
  7539                                  ; Function:
  7540                                  ;	give users an idea of what country the application is running
  7541                                  ; Outputs:
  7542                                  ;	IF DX != -1 on input (get country)
  7543                                  ;	  AL = 0 means return current country table.
  7544                                  ;	  0<AL<0FFH means return country table for country AL
  7545                                  ;	  AL = 0FF means return country table for country BX
  7546                                  ;	  No Carry:
  7547                                  ;	     Register BX will contain the 16-bit country code.
  7548                                  ;	     Register AL will contain the low 8 bits of the country code.
  7549                                  ;	     The block pointed to by DS:DX is filled in with the information
  7550                                  ;	     for the particular country.
  7551                                  ;		BYTE  Size of this table excluding this byte and the next
  7552                                  ;		BYTE  Country code represented by this table
  7553                                  ;			A sequence of n bytes, where n is the number specified
  7554                                  ;			by the first byte above and is not > internat_block_max,
  7555                                  ;			in the correct order for being returned by the
  7556                                  ;			INTERNATIONAL call as follows:
  7557                                  ;		WORD	Date format 0=mdy, 1=dmy, 2=ymd
  7558                                  ;		5 BYTE	Currency symbol null terminated
  7559                                  ;		2 BYTE	thousands separator null terminated
  7560                                  ;		2 BYTE	Decimal point null terminated
  7561                                  ;		2 BYTE	Date separator null terminated
  7562                                  ;		2 BYTE	Time separator null terminated
  7563                                  ;		1 BYTE	Bit field.  Currency format.
  7564                                  ;			Bit 0.	=0 $ before #  =1 $ after #
  7565                                  ;			Bit 1.	no. of spaces between # and $ (0 or 1)
  7566                                  ;		1 BYTE	No. of significant decimal digits in currency
  7567                                  ;		1 BYTE	Bit field.  Time format.
  7568                                  ;			Bit 0.	=0 12 hour clock  =1 24 hour
  7569                                  ;		DWORD	Call address of case conversion routine
  7570                                  ;		2 BYTE	Data list separator null terminated.
  7571                                  ;	  Carry:
  7572                                  ;	     Register AX has the error code.
  7573                                  ;	IF DX = -1 on input (set current country)
  7574                                  ;	  AL = 0 is an error
  7575                                  ;	  0<AL<0FFH means set current country to country AL
  7576                                  ;	  AL = 0FF means set current country to country BX
  7577                                  ;	  No Carry:
  7578                                  ;	    Current country SET
  7579                                  ;	    Register AL will contain the low 8 bits of the country code.
  7580                                  ;	  Carry:
  7581                                  ;	     Register AX has the error code.
  7582                                  ;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  7583

  7856                                  ;
  7857                                  ; Procedure Name : $GetExtCntry
  7858                                  ;

  9261                                  ;BREAK <$Parse_File_Descriptor -- Parse an arbitrary string into an FCB>
  9262                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9263                                  ; Inputs:
  9264                                  ;       DS:SI Points to a command line
  9265                                  ;       ES:DI Points to an empty FCB
  9266                                  ;       Bit 0 of AL = 1 At most one leading separator scanned off
  9267                                  ;                   = 0 Parse stops if separator encountered
  9268                                  ;       Bit 1 of AL = 1 If drive field blank in command line - leave FCB
  9269                                  ;                   = 0  "    "    "     "         "      "  - put 0 in FCB
  9270                                  ;       Bit 2 of AL = 1 If filename field blank - leave FCB
  9271                                  ;                   = 0  "       "      "       - put blanks in FCB
  9272                                  ;       Bit 3 of AL = 1 If extension field blank - leave FCB
  9273                                  ;                   = 0  "       "      "        - put blanks in FCB
  9274                                  ; Function:
  9275                                  ;       Parse command line into FCB
  9276                                  ; Returns:
  9277                                  ;       AL = 1 if '*' or '?' in filename or extension, 0 otherwise
  9278                                  ;       DS:SI points to first character after filename
  9279                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9280                                  
  9281                                  	; 13/01/2024
  9282                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:51BFh
  9283                                  	; MSDOS 6.22 MSDOS.SYS - DOSCODE:4D22h
  9284                                  
  9285                                  _$PARSE_FILE_DESCRIPTOR:
  9286 000012C3 E8EE45                  	call	MAKEFCB
  9287 000012C6 56                      	PUSH    SI
  9288 000012C7 E8C1F1                  	call	Get_User_Stack
  9289                                  	;pop	word [si+8]
  9290 000012CA 8F4408                  	POP     word [SI+user_env.user_SI]
  9291 000012CD C3                      	retn
  9292

 10055                                  	inc	bx
 10056                                  	;INC	AX			; +2 (reserved), -1 (count -> max)
 10057                                  ;
 10058                                  ;	There has been a bug in our fatsize calculation for so long
 10059                                  ;	  that we can't correct it now without causing some user to
 10060                                  ;	  experience data loss. There are even cases where allowing
 10061                                  ;	  the number of clusters to exceed the fats is the optimal
 10062                                  ;	  case -- where adding 2 more fat sectors would make the
 10063                                  ;	  data field smaller so that there's nothing to use the extra
 10064                                  ;	  fat sectors for.
 10065                                  ;
 10066                                  ;	Note that this bug had very minor known symptoms. CHKDSK would
 10067                                  ;	  still report that there was a cluster left when the disk was
 10068                                  ;	  actually full. Very graceful failure for a corrupt system
 10069                                  ;	  configuration. There may be worse cases that were never
 10070                                  ;	  properly traced back to this bug. The problem cases only
 10071                                  ;	  occurred when partition sizes were very near FAT sector
 10072                                  ;	  rounding boundaries, which were rare cases.
 10073                                  ;
 10074                                  ;	Also, it's possible that some third-party partition program might
 10075                                  ;	  create a partition that had a less-than-perfect FAT calculation
 10076                                  ;	  scheme. In this hypothetical case, the number of allocation
 10077                                  ;	  clusters which don't actually have FAT entries to represent
 10078                                  ;	  them might be larger and might create a more catastrophic
 10079                                  ;	  failure. So we'll provide the safeguard of limiting the
 10080                                  ;	  max_cluster to the amount that will fit in the FATs.
 10081                                  ;
 10082                                  ;	ax = maximum legal cluster, ES:BP -> dpb
 10083                                  
 10084                                  ;	make sure the number of fat sectors is actually enough to
 10085                                  ;	  hold that many clusters. otherwise, back the number of
 10086                                  ;	  clusters down
 10087                                  
 10088                                  	; 15/12/2022
 10089                                  	; bx = number of clusters
 10090

 10695                                  	; (MSDOS 6.0 note)
 10696                                  	;
 10697                                  	; The address in BX:AX will be F01D:FEF0 if there is 64K or more 
 10698                                  	; memory in the system. This is equivalent to 0:c0 if A20 is OFF.
 10699                                  	; If DOS is in HMA this equivalence is no longer valid as A20 is ON.
 10700                                  	; But the BIOS which now resides in FFFF:30 has 5 bytes in FFFF:D0
 10701                                  	; (F01D:FEF0) which is the same as the ones in 0:C0, thereby 
 10702                                  	; making this equvalence valid for this particular case. If however
 10703                                  	; there is less than 64K remaining the address in BX:AX will not 
 10704                                  	; be the same as above. We will then stuff 0:c0, the call 5 address
 10705                                  	; into the PSP.
 10706                                  	;
 10707                                  	; Therefore for the case where there is less than 64K remaining in 
 10708                                  	; the system old CPM Apps that look at PSP:6 to determine memory
 10709                                  	; requirements will not work. Call 5, however will continue to work
 10710                                  	; for all cases.
 10711                                  	;
 10712                                  
 10713                                  	;mov	[6],ax
 10714                                  	;mov	[8],bx

 10890                                  ;

 10892                                  ;	     Strings of different lengths don't match.

 11451                                  ; Some old versions of the 80286 have a bug in the chip. The popf instruction

 11453                                  ; disabled and you need a popf instruction use the 'popff' macro instead.
 11454                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

 11457                                  ;	jmp	$+3
 11458                                  ;	iret
 11459                                  ;	push	cs

 11923                                  
 11924                                  ;**	Standard device IO for MSDOS (first 12 function calls)
 11925                                  ;
 11926                                  ;	TITLE	IBMCPMIO - device IO for MSDOS
 11927                                  ;	NAME	IBMCPMIO
 11928                                  
 11929                                  ;	Old style CP/M 1-12 system calls to talk to reserved devices
 11930                                  ;
 11931                                  ;	$Std_Con_Input_No_Echo
 11932                                  ;	$Std_Con_String_Output
 11933                                  ;	$Std_Con_String_Input
 11934                                  ;	$RawConIO
 11935                                  ;	$RawConInput
 11936                                  ;	RAWOUT
 11937                                  ;	RAWOUT2
 11938                                  ;
 11939                                  
 11940                                  ; The following routines form the console I/O group (funcs 1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11).
 11941                                  ; They assume ES and DS NOTHING, while not strictly correct, this forces data
 11942                                  ; references to be SS or CS relative which is desired.
 11943

 11972                                  ; The following routines form the console I/O group (funcs 1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11).
 11973                                  ; They assume ES and DS NOTHING, while not strictly correct, this forces data
 11974                                  ; references to be SS or CS relative which is desired.
 11975                                  
 11976                                  ;DOSCODE SEGMENT
 11977                                  ;	ASSUME	SS:DOSDATA,CS:DOSCODE
 11978                                  
 11979                                  
 11980                                  ;hkn; 	All the variables use SS override or DS. Therefore there is
 11981                                  ;hkn;	no need to specifically set up any seg regs unless SS assumption is
 11982                                  ;hkn;	not valid. 
 11983                                  
 11984                                  ; DOSCODE:51BAh (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 11985                                  ; 08/11/2022
 11986                                  ; DOSCODE:51A6h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)

 11996                                  _$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO:   ;System call 8
 11997                                  
 11998                                  ; Inputs:
 11999                                  ;	None
 12000                                  ; Function:
 12001                                  ;	Input character from console, no echo
 12002                                  ; Returns:
 12003                                  ;	AL = character
 12004                                  
 12005 000018F8 1E                      	push	ds
 12006 000018F9 56                      	push	si
 12007                                  INTEST:
 12008 000018FA E80542                  	call	STATCHK
 12009 000018FD 753A                    	jnz	short GET ; 08/09/2018
 12010                                  ;*************************************************************************
 12011                                  ;hkn; SS override
 12012 000018FF 36803E[A00A]00          	cmp	byte [SS:PRINTER_FLAG],0  ; is printer idle?
 12013 00001905 7505                    	jnz	short no_sys_wait
 12014 00001907 B405                    	mov	ah,5			; get input status with system wait
 12015 00001909 E84934                  	call	IOFUNC
 12016                                  no_sys_wait:
 12017                                  ;**************************************************************************
 12018 0000190C B484                    	MOV	AH,84h		; (Microsoft Networks - KEYBOARD BUSY LOOP)
 12019 0000190E CD2A                    	INT	int_IBM	 ; int 2Ah
 12020                                  
 12021                                  ;;; 7/15/86  update the date in the idle loop
 12022                                  ;;; Dec 19, 1986 D.C.L. changed following CMP to Byte Ptr from Word Ptr
 12023                                  ;;;;		 to shorten loop in consideration of the PC Convertible
 12024                                  
 12025                                  ;hkn; SS override
 12026 00001910 36803E[BD0D]FF          	CMP	byte [SS:DATE_FLAG],-1	; date is updated may be every
 12027 00001916 751A                    	JNZ	short NoUpdate		; 65535 x ? ms if no one calls
 12028                                  
 12029 00001918 50                      	PUSH	AX
 12030 00001919 53                      	PUSH	BX			; following is tricky,
 12031 0000191A 51                      	PUSH	CX			; it may be called by critical handler
 12032 0000191B 52                      	PUSH	DX			; at that time, DEVCALL is used by
 12033                                  					; other's READ or WRITE
 12034 0000191C 1E                      	PUSH	DS			; save DS = SFT's segment
 12035                                  
 12036                                  ;hkn; READTIME must use ds = DOSDATA
 12037                                  ;hkn;	PUSH	CS			; READTIME must use DS=CS
 12038                                  
 12039 0000191D 16                      	PUSH	SS ; 04/05/2019
 12040 0000191E 1F                      	POP	DS
 12041                                  
 12042                                  	;MOV	AX,0			; therefore, we save DEVCALL
 12043                                  	; 26/06/2024
 12044 0000191F 31C0                    	xor	ax,ax
 12045 00001921 E89A02                  	CALL	Save_Restore_Packet	; save DEVCALL packet
 12046                                  	;invoke	READTIME		; readtime
 12047 00001924 E854F2                  	call	READTIME
 12048 00001927 B80100                  	MOV	AX,1
 12049 0000192A E89102                  	CALL	Save_Restore_Packet	; restore DEVCALL packet
 12050                                  
 12051                                  ;	; MSDOS 3.3 (IBMDOS.COM, Offset 1F8Ch)
 12052                                  ;	; (MSDOS 6.0 code does not contain IBM DOS FETCHI_TAG check)
 12053                                  ;	push	bx
 12054                                  ;	mov	bx,DATE_FLAG
 12055                                  ;	add	bx,2  ; mov bx,FETCHI_FLAG
 12056                                  ;	cmp	word [cs:bx],5872h
 12057                                  ;	jz	short FETCHI_TAG_chk_ok
 12058                                  ;	call	DOSINIT
 12059                                  ;FETCHI_TAG_chk_ok:
 12060                                  ;	pop	bx
 12061                                  
 12062 0000192D 1F                      	POP	DS			; restore DS
 12063 0000192E 5A                      	POP	DX
 12064 0000192F 59                      	POP	CX
 12065 00001930 5B                      	POP	BX
 12066 00001931 58                      	POP	AX
 12067                                  NoUpdate:
 12068                                  
 12069                                  ;hkn; SS override
 12070 00001932 36FF06[BD0D]            	INC	word [SS:DATE_FLAG]
 12071                                  
 12072                                  ;;; 7/15/86 ;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
 12073 00001937 EBC1                    	JMP	short INTEST
 12074                                  GET:
 12075 00001939 30E4                    	XOR	AH,AH
 12076 0000193B E81734                  	call	IOFUNC
 12077 0000193E 5E                      	POP	SI
 12078 0000193F 1F                      	POP	DS
 12079                                  ;;; 7/15/86
 12080                                  
 12081                                  ;hkn; SS override
 12082                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 12083 00001940 36C606[BC0D]00          	MOV	BYTE [SS:SCAN_FLAG],0
 12084                                  	;
 12085 00001946 3C00                    	CMP	AL,0	    ; extended code ( AL )
 12086 00001948 7505                    	JNZ	short noscan
 12087

 12089                                  	;MOV	BYTE [SS:SCAN_FLAG],1 ; set this flag for ALT_Q key
 12090                                  	; 20/06/2023
 12091 0000194A 36FE06[BC0D]            	inc	byte [SS:SCAN_FLAG]
 12092                                  noscan:
 12093 0000194F C3                      	retn

 12117                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12118                                  ;
 12119                                  ;**	$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT - Input Line from Console
 12120                                  ;
 12121                                  ;	$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT Fills a buffer from console input until CR
 12122                                  ;
 12123                                  ;	ENTRY	(ds:dx) = input buffer
 12124                                  ;	EXIT	none
 12125                                  ;	USES	ALL
 12126                                  ;
 12127                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12128                                  
 12129                                  	; 15/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
 12130                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:58D4h
 12131                                  
 12132                                  _$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT:		;System call 10
 12133                                  
 12134                                  	; 15/01/2024
 12135                                  	;mov	ax,ss
 12136                                  	;mov	es,ax
 12137 0000195C 16                      	push	ss
 12138 0000195D 07                      	pop	es
 12139                                  
 12140 0000195E 89D6                    	mov	si,dx
 12141 00001960 30ED                    	xor	ch,ch
 12142 00001962 AD                      	lodsw
 12143                                  
 12144                                  ;	(AL) = the buffer length
 12145                                  ;	(AH) = the template length
 12146                                  
 12147 00001963 08C0                            or	al,al
 12148 00001965 74E8                            jz	short noscan	;Buffer is 0 length!!?
 12149 00001967 88E3                    	mov	bl,ah		;Init template counter
 12150 00001969 88EF                            mov	bh,ch		;Init template counter
 12151                                  
 12152                                  ;	(BL) = the number of bytes in the template
 12153                                  
 12154 0000196B 38D8                            cmp	al,bl
 12155 0000196D 7605                            jbe	short NOEDIT	;If length of buffer inconsistent with contents
 12156 0000196F 80380D                          cmp	byte [bx+si],c_CR ; 0Dh
 12157 00001972 7402                            jz	short EDITON	;If CR correctly placed EDIT is OK
 12158                                  
 12159                                  ; The number of chars in the template is >= the number of chars in buffer or
 12160                                  ; there is no CR at the end of the template. This is an inconsistant state
 12161                                  ; of affairs. Pretend that the template was empty:
 12162                                  ;
 12163                                  
 12164                                  NOEDIT:	
 12165 00001974 88EB                    	mov	bl,ch		;Reset buffer
 12166                                  EDITON: 
 12167 00001976 88C2                    	mov	dl,al
 12168 00001978 4A                      	dec	dx		;DL is # of bytes we can put in the buffer
 12169                                  
 12170                                  ;	Top level. We begin to read a line in.
 12171                                  
 12172                                  NEWLIN: 
 12173 00001979 36A0[F901]              	mov	al,[SS:CARPOS]
 12174 0000197D 36A2[FA01]              	mov	[SS:STARTPOS],al ;Remember position in raw buffer
 12175                                  
 12176 00001981 56                      	push	si
 12177 00001982 BF[FB01]                	mov	di,INBUF ;Build the new line here
 12178 00001985 36882E[7905]            	mov	byte [SS:INSMODE],ch ;Insert mode off
 12179 0000198A 88EF                    	mov	bh,ch		;No chars from template yet
 12180 0000198C 88EE                    	mov	dh,ch		;No chars to new line yet
 12181 0000198E E867FF                  	call	_$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO ;Get first char
 12182 00001991 3C0A                    	cmp	al,c_LF		; 0Ah	;Linefeed 
 12183 00001993 7503                    	jnz	short GOTCH
 12184                                  
 12185                                  ;	This is the main loop of reading in a character and processing it.
 12186                                  ;
 12187                                  ;	(BH) = the index of the next byte in the template
 12188                                  ;	(BL) = the length of the template
 12189                                  ;	(DH) = the number of bytes in the buffer
 12190                                  ;	(DL) = the length of the buffer
 12191                                  
 12192                                  GETCH:
 12193 00001995 E860FF                  	call	_$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO
 12194                                  GOTCH:
 12195                                  ;
 12196                                  ; Brain-damaged Tim Patterson ignored ^F in case his BIOS did not flush the
 12197                                  ; input queue.
 12198                                  ;
 12199 00001998 3C06                            cmp	al,"F"-"@"  ; CMP AL, 6  ; Ignore ^F
 12200 0000199A 74F9                    	jz	short GETCH
 12201                                  
 12202                                  ;	If the leading char is the function-key lead byte
 12203                                  
 12204                                  	;cmp	al,[SS:ESCCHAR]
 12205                                  
 12206                                  	; 04/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 12207                                  
 12208                                  ;hkn; 	ESCCHAR is in TABLE seg (DOSCODE)
 12209                                  
 12210 0000199C 2E3A06[850A]            	CMP	AL,[cs:ESCCHAR]
 12211 000019A1 7439                            jz	short ESCAPE	;change reserved keyword DBM 5-7-87
 12212                                  
 12213                                  ;	Rubout and ^H are both destructive backspaces.
 12214                                  
 12215 000019A3 3C7F                            cmp	al,c_DEL ; 7FH
 12216                                          ;jz	short BACKSPJ
 12217                                          ; 15/01/2024
 12218 000019A5 7466                    	je	short BACKSP
 12219 000019A7 3C08                    	cmp	al,c_BS  ; 8
 12220                                          ;jz	short BACKSPJ
 12221                                          ; 15/01/2024
 12222 000019A9 7462                    	je	short BACKSP
 12223                                  
 12224                                  	; 04/05/2019 -	MSDOS 6.0, also MSDOS 6.21 has bug (bullshit) here.
 12225                                  	;		Two NOPs -instead of a JMP short, as two bytes-
 12226                                  	;	   	after CMP and a CMP again!
 12227                                  	;		
 12228                                  	;		-It would be better if they use a 'JMP short' to 
 12229                                  	;	      	DOSCODE:5279h from DOSCODE:5271h and leave NOPs
 12230                                  	;		between them. Then, they would be able use a patch
 12231                                  	;		between 5271h and 5279h when if it will be required.
 12232                                  	;		I think Tim Patterson would not do this CMP mistake!-
 12233                                  	;	
 12234                                  	; (MSDOS.SYS, from DOSCODE:5271h to DOSCODE:5279h)
 12235                                  
 12236                                  	; 08/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 12237                                  	;
 12238                                  	; (Note: nops below might be used for patching code for Windows 3.1)
 12239                                  
 12240                                  ;DOSCODE:526D	cmp     al, 8
 12241                                  ;DOSCODE:526F	jz      short BACKSPJ
 12242                                  ;DOSCODE:5271	cmp     al, 17h
 12243                                  ;DOSCODE:5273	nop
 12244                                  ;DOSCODE:5274	nop
 12245                                  ;DOSCODE:5275	cmp     al, 15h
 12246                                  ;DOSCODE:5277	nop
 12247                                  ;DOSCODE:5278	nop
 12248                                  ;DOSCODE:5279	cmp     al, 0Dh
 12249                                  ;DOSCODE:527B	jz      short ENDLIN
 12250                                  ;DOSCODE:527D	cmp     al, 0Ah
 12251                                  ;DOSCODE:527F	jz      short PHYCRLF
 12252                                  	
 12253                                  	; 08/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 12254                                  	; DOSCODE:525Dh
 12255                                  
 12256                                  ; 16/12/2022
 12257                                  %if 0
 12258                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 12259                                  ;	^W deletes backward once and then backs up until a letter is before the
 12260                                  ;	cursor
 12261                                  
 12262                                  	CMP     AL,"W"-"@" ; 17h
 12263                                  
 12264                                  ;	The removal of the comment characters before the jump statement will
 12265                                  ;	cause ^W to backup a word.
 12266                                  
 12267                                  ;***	JZ	short WordDel
 12268                                  	NOP
 12269                                  	NOP
 12270                                  
 12271                                  	CMP     AL,"U"-"@" ; 15h
 12272                                  
 12273                                  ;	The removal of the comment characters before the jump statement will
 12274                                  ;	cause ^U to clear a line.
 12275                                  
 12276                                  ;***	JZ	short LineDel
 12277                                  	NOP
 12278                                  	NOP
 12279                                  
 12280                                  %endif
 12281                                  
 12282                                  ;	CR terminates the line.
 12283                                  
 12284 000019AB 3C0D                            cmp	al,c_CR ; 0Dh
 12285 000019AD 7430                            jz	short ENDLIN
 12286                                  
 12287                                  ;	LF goes to a new line and keeps on reading.
 12288                                  
 12289 000019AF 3C0A                            cmp	al,c_LF ; 0Ah
 12290 000019B1 7442                    	jz	short PHYCRLF
 12291                                  
 12292                                  ;	^X (or ESC) deletes the line and starts over
 12293                                  
 12294                                  	; MSDOS 3.3
 12295                                  	;cmp	al,[ss:CANCHAR] ; 1Bh
 12296                                  	;jz	short KILNEW
 12297                                  
 12298                                  	; MSDOS 6.0 (& MSDOS 6.21)
 12299                                  
 12300                                  ;hkn; 	CANCHAR is in TABLE seg (DOSCODE), so CS override
 12301                                  
 12302 000019B3 2E3A06[840A]            	cmp	al,[cs:CANCHAR] ; 1Bh
 12303 000019B8 7440                    	jz	short KILNEW
 12304                                  	
 12305                                  	;cmp	al,CANCEL ; 1Bh	; Retro DOS v3.0
 12306                                  	;jz	short KILNEW
 12307                                  
 12308                                  ; Otherwise, we save the input character.
 12309                                  
 12310                                  SAVCH:	
 12311 000019BA 38D6                    	cmp	dh,dl
 12312 000019BC 7317                    	jnb	short BUFFUL		; buffer is full.
 12313 000019BE AA                              stosb
 12314 000019BF FEC6                    	inc	dh                      ; increment count in buffer.
 12315 000019C1 E8B702                  	call	BUFOUT			; Print control chars nicely
 12316                                  
 12317 000019C4 36803E[7905]00                  cmp	byte [SS:INSMODE], 0
 12318 000019CA 75C9                    	jnz	short GETCH		; insertmode => don't advance template
 12319 000019CC 38DF                            cmp	bh,bl
 12320 000019CE 73C5                            jnb	short GETCH		; no more characters in template
 12321 000019D0 46                              inc	si                      ; Skip to next char in template
 12322 000019D1 FEC7                            inc	bh                      ; remember position in template
 12323 000019D3 EBC0                            jmp	short GETCH
 12324                                  
 12325                                  	; 15/01/2024
 12326                                  ;BACKSPJ: 
 12327                                  	;jmp	short BACKSP
 12328                                  
 12329                                  BUFFUL: 
 12330 000019D5 B007                    	mov	al, 7			; Bell to signal full buffer
 12331 000019D7 E80D02                  	call	OUTT
 12332 000019DA EBB9                    	jmp	short GETCH
 12333                                  
 12334                                  ESCAPE: 
 12335                                  	;transfer OEMFunctionKey
 12336 000019DC E9D1F0                  	JMP	OEMFunctionKey		; let the OEM's handle the key dispatch
 12337                                  
 12338                                  ENDLIN:
 12339 000019DF AA                              stosb				; Put the CR in the buffer
 12340 000019E0 E80402                  	call	OUTT                    ; Echo it
 12341 000019E3 5F                              pop	di                      ; Get start of user buffer
 12342 000019E4 8875FF                          mov	[di-1], dh		; Tell user how many bytes
 12343 000019E7 FEC6                            inc	dh			; DH is length including CR
 12344                                  
 12345                                  COPYNEW:
 12346                                  	; (IBMDOS.COM, MSDOS 2.0, STRIN.ASM)
 12347                                  	;mov	bp, es
 12348                                  	;mov	bx, ds
 12349                                  	;mov	es, bx
 12350                                  	;mov	ds, bp
 12351                                  	;mov	si, INBUF
 12352                                  	;mov	cl, dh
 12353                                  	;rep	movsb
 12354                                  	;retn
 12355                                  
 12356                                  	; CPMIO.ASM (MSDOS 6.0)
 12357                                  	; (IBMDOS.COM, MSDOS 3.3, Offset 2061h) 
 12358                                  	;SAVE	<DS,ES>
 12359 000019E9 1E                      	PUSH	DS
 12360 000019EA 06                      	PUSH	ES
 12361                                  	;RESTORE <DS,ES>		; XCHG ES,DS
 12362 000019EB 1F                      	POP	DS
 12363 000019EC 07                      	POP	ES
 12364                                  
 12365                                  ;;hkn; INBUF is in DOSDATA
 12366 000019ED BE[FB01]                        MOV     SI,INBUF
 12367 000019F0 88F1                            MOV     CL,DH                   ; set up count
 12368 000019F2 F3A4                            REP     MOVSB                   ; Copy final line to user buffer
 12369                                  OLDBAK_RETN:
 12370 000019F4 C3                              RETN
 12371

 12373

 12451                                  ; DOSCODE:52F3h (MSDOS 621, MSDOS.SYS)
 12452                                  
 12453                                  ; The user wants to throw away what he's typed in and wants to start over.
 12454                                  ; We print the backslash and then go to the next line and tab to the correct
 12455                                  ; spot to begin the buffered input.
 12456                                  
 12457                                  KILNEW:
 12458 000019FA B05C                            mov	al,'\'
 12459 000019FC E8E801                          call	OUTT            ;Print the CANCEL indicator
 12460 000019FF 5E                              pop	si		;Remember start of edit buffer
 12461                                  PUTNEW:
 12462 00001A00 E81001                  	call	CRLF            ;Go to next line on screen
 12463 00001A03 36A0[FA01]              	mov	al,[SS:STARTPOS]
 12464 00001A07 E85102                  	call	TAB             ;Tab over
 12465 00001A0A E96CFF                          JMP     NEWLIN		;Start over again
 12466                                  
 12467                                  ;	Destructively back up one character position
 12468                                  
 12469                                  BACKSP:
 12470                                  	; 09/09/2018
 12471 00001A0D E80800                  	Call    BackSpace
 12472 00001A10 EB83                    	JMP     short GETCH	; 15/01/2024
 12473                                  
 12474                                  	; 15/01/2024
 12475                                  ;User really wants an ESC character in his line
 12476                                  TWOESC:	
 12477 00001A12 2EA0[850A]              	mov	al,[cs:ESCCHAR] ; 10/06/2019
 12478 00001A16 EBA2                    	jmp	short SAVCH
 12479                                  
 12480                                  BackSpace:
 12481 00001A18 08F6                    	or	dh,dh
 12482 00001A1A 7419                    	jz	short OLDBAK	;No chars in line, do nothing to line
 12483 00001A1C E85800                  	call	BACKUP          ;Do the backup

 13469                                  ;Break <$Get_FCB_Position - set random record fields to current pos>
 13470                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13471                                  ;
 13472                                  ;   $Get_FCB_Position - look at an FCB, retrieve the current position from the
 13473                                  ;	extent and next record field and set the random record field to point
 13474                                  ;	to that record
 13475                                  ;
 13476                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:DX point to a possible extended FCB
 13477                                  ;   Outputs:	The random record field of the FCB is set to the current record
 13478                                  ;   Registers modified: all
 13479                                  ;
 13480                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13481                                  ;
 13482                                  
 13483                                  _$GET_FCB_POSITION:
 13484 00001D02 E8FB04                  	call	GetExtended		; point to FCB
 13485 00001D05 E8CC04                  	call	GetExtent		; DX:AX is current record
 13486                                  	;mov	[si+21h],ax
 13487 00001D08 894421                  	MOV	[SI+SYS_FCB.RR],AX 	; drop in low order piece
 13488                                  	;mov	[si+23h],dl
 13489 00001D0B 885423                  	MOV	[SI+SYS_FCB.RR+2],DL	; drop in high order piece
 13490                                  	;cmp	word [si+0Eh],64
 13491 00001D0E 837C0E40                	CMP	word [SI+SYS_FCB.RECSIZ],64
